beats.text: You walk into the kitchen. And then... why are you here?
You're not losing it. There's a name for this.
Your brain files what you're doing as an event. Like a little scene.
A doorway tells your brain: new scene. So it tidies up the old one.
In a 2011 study, people carried objects through rooms.
After walking through a door, they forgot more than after walking the same distance in one room.
And walking back into the first room didn't fix it.
A 2021 study added a twist. Doorways mostly hurt memory when people's heads were already busy.
So if this happens a lot, you're not forgetful. You're just carrying a lot.

sources: Radvansky, Krawietz & Tamplin (2011). Walking through doorways causes forgetting. QJEP. Virtual and real rooms; worse memory after a doorway than after the same distance within a room; returning to the original room did not restore it.

McFadyen, Nolan, Pinocy, Buteri, Baumann (2021). Doorways do not always cause forgetting. BMC Psychology. VR: no doorway effect without extra load (n=29); with a demanding counting task, doorways impaired memory (n=45).
